To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intensity of the Cu Kα and Kβ lines increases linearly with the number of electrons emitted by the cathode of the X-ray tube until a certain critical number of electrons is reached.
The intensity of the Cu Kα and Cu Kβ lines increases proportionally to the current up to 4 mA, and then the increase in intensity is linear.

the intensity of the Kα and Kβ lines of copper is proportional to the number of electrons striking the target up to about 4 mA of current, at which point the proportionality ceases and a new linear relationship is established.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the intensity of the characteristic lines Cu Kα and Cu Kβ in the X-ray spectrum as a function of the number of electrons emitted from the cathode.
the dependence of the intensity of X-ray spectral lines on the number of cathode electrons.
the dependence of the intensity of the characteristic lines of the x-ray spectrum of copper on the number of electrons emitted by the cathode of an x-ray tube.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dependence of the intensity of the characteristic X-ray lines on the number of the electrons which are producing them is linear up to a certain value of the number of electrons, which is not dependent on the voltage applied to the tube.
the intensity of a line is proportional to the number of cathode electrons up to the point of the saturation of the line intensity.

the intensity of the Kα and Kβ Cu lines increases proportionately up to 4 mA of anode current, and then ceases to be so, but that there exists again a linear relation between the intensity of the lines and the anode current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intensity of X-ray spectral lines is proportional to the number of electrons which are responsible for the production of the lines.
the intensity of the Kα and Kβ Cu lines increases with the number of electrons, up to 4 mA, in a linear way.
the intensity of the characteristic X-ray lines Cu Kα and Cu Kβ increases proportionally to the current strength in a certain range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intensity of the X-ray lines is not a monotonic function of the electron current.
the number of electrons in the cathode determines the intensity of the emitted X-ray lines.
